messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — anomaly detected: model redwood-rlhf-v2 serving in us-east-1 showing a 12% increase in hallucination/regression score on prod-evals/full-regression-run. Trigger: quality-regression-signal. Pager dispatched to kevin (oncall). :rotating_light:

kevin (oncall): Got it. I'm on the pager. tagging @maria and @sam for triage. Initial question: is this a data, model, or infra regression?

maria (sre): I'm pulling service logs and routing metrics now. No infra alerts (CPU/GPU mem) in the region. We've got increased 500s in the model-serving layer starting ~1839499000.

sam (ml-engineer): Thanks. I'll run quick diffs between v1.3.2 and v2 weight changes and check for obvious tokenization or calibration shifts. Can someone confirm cohort where eval failed?

kevin (oncall): Triage note: regression primarily shows up on conversational QA prompt set (prod-evals/qa-edge-cases). Customer-facing inference latency unaffected, but quality drop affects 4% of calls in the sample window.

maria (sre): Copy. Exported a sample of failed requests to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1839501123/failed-samples.tar.gz. Permissions: incidents-read.

sam (ml-engineer): Reviewing samples. Looks like new decoding tweak in v2 changed end-of-sentence behavior; several answers are truncated or drop qualifiers. Hypothesis: beam/penalty defaults in v2 unintentionally different.

kevin (oncall): Given customer impact (quality, not availability) and quick hypothesis, I propose immediate mitigation: pin traffic to last-known-good model redwood-rlhf-v1.3.2 in us-east-1 and open a rollback of the v2 rollout. Can we do a staged pin and keep v2 in cold standby?

maria (sre): Agreed. I'll apply routing pin. Doing canary-to-stable switch now.

ops-bot: ACTION LOGGED — routing-change requested by kevin (oncall). Command queued:
```
redwoodctl route update --region us-east-1 --model redwood-rlhf-v1.3.2 --weight 100 --note "rollback due to quality regression"
```

maria (sre): Running the command now...

ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE SUCCESS — redwood-rlhf-v1.3.2 now serving 100% traffic in us-east-1. Change id: rout-20230401-0923.

kevin (oncall): Confirming metrics — quality error rate on the failing eval set dropped back to baseline within two minutes. :thumbsup:

sam (ml-engineer): Good catch. I'll create a quick repro job to reproduce the truncation locally and file a model rollback/patch PR. Tracker: MLP-4213.

kevin (oncall): Drafting status page and customer comms. Posting suggested copy here for review. Please keep edits minimal; we'll push once approved by product-ops.

product-ops: Paste your drafts, will sign off quickly.

kevin (oncall): STATUS PAGE DRAFT:
```
Summary: We experienced a short-lived model quality regression impacting generation accuracy for some customers using the redwood-rlhf-v2 model in the us-east-1 region.
Impact: A subset of requests (approx 4%) saw degraded response quality (truncation or incorrect completions). Latency and availability were unaffected.
Action taken: We pinned traffic back to redwood-rlhf-v1.3.2 and rolled back the v2 rollout in region us-east-1 at 2023-04-01T09:23Z. Engineers are investigating root cause and preparing a fixed model rollout.
Current status: Mitigated — traffic is on v1.3.2; monitoring continues.
Next update: in 2 hours or when we have more details.
```

product-ops: Fine with that, minor edit: remove exact percent on public page, change to "a small percentage" for cautious wording.

kevin (oncall): Updated. Customer-facing email draft (short):
```
Hi <CustomerName>,

We detected a temporary quality regression affecting the redwood-rlhf-v2 model in us-east-1. We routed traffic back to the previously-stable model; your service availability was not impacted. Our team is investigating and will follow up with root cause and timeline for a safe re-release.

If you saw incorrect completions and would like the samples investigated, reply and we can pull logs.

Apologies for the disruption.
— Redwood Inference Support
```

lucy (cust-success): I'll queue targeted emails to customers known to be using redwood-rlhf-v2 in us-east-1 and offer log review. Will personalize for top 10 accounts.

kevin (oncall): Internal short-form comm (for slack/internal):
"We rolled back rlhf-v2 in us-east-1 due to a decoding/truncation regression. Traffic pinned to v1.3.2. Sam owning model repro and fix. Maria monitored routing. Kevin handled pager. Emma will take next shift."

emma (oncall-next): Taking handoff at 2023-04-01T10:00Z. Handoff notes:
- Incident id: INC-1839501123
- Mitigation: traffic pinned to redwood-rlhf-v1.3.2 in us-east-1
- Follow-ups: sam to provide repro + PR, maria to keep monitoring 1h, product-ops to approve customer copy
- Links: S3 samples (s3://redwood-incidents/1839501123/failed-samples.tar.gz), routing change id rout-20230401-0923, ticket MLP-4213

kevin (oncall): Adding checklist for you, emma:
1) Verify route is still pinned and no rollouts are scheduled.
2) Confirm alerting thresholds on quality regressions are suppressed for controlled investigation (don't auto-rollback other models).
3) If any customer escalations arrive, route to lucy/cs.

emma (oncall-next): Got it. I'll monitor and will escalate to oncall-squad if we see any reappearance.

sam (ml-engineer): Quick note for postmortem template — propose the following sections: timeline, impact, mitigation steps, root cause hypothesis, fix plan, rollout checklist (include sample-based QA, regen of evaluation corpora, and gated canary with manual QA). I'll draft MLP-4213 PR and link tests.

product-ops: Also flag legal/compliance for any regulated customers we must notify separately. I'll draft the formal customer notice and share with lucy.

kevin (oncall): Closing log: mitigation successful, pinned model, customers notified (targeted). Leaving incident in monitoring state. Will open a postmortem draft once sam's repro is in.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status changed to "Mitigated" by kevin (oncall) at 1839501600.

lucy (cust-success): Sent top-10 customer emails with the short template at 2023-04-01T09:30Z. Will follow up per replies.

product-ops: Please avoid naming internal model weight roll numbers in public comms. Use model alias (e.g., redwood-rlhf stable) on status page/email.

kevin (oncall): Noted and updated public copy accordingly.

maria (sre): Monitoring 20 minutes post-roll; quality metrics stable. No further action required unless trend reappears.

sam (ml-engineer): Uploaded repro notebook and initial debug notes to GH: https://git.redwood.ai/ml/MLP-4213 (private). Draft PR opened.

kevin (oncall): Thanks team. Emma — you're the handoff owner. If nothing degrades in the next hour, we'll move to post-incident review and pick a target window for re-release testing with stricter QA gates.

emma (oncall-next): Acknowledged. Taking watch. :raised_hands:

kevin (oncall): Final: saving incident artifacts and marking for postmortem scheduling. Closing as mitigated in channel, leaving thread open for follow-ups.

ops-bot: THREAD ANNOTATION — artifacts saved: routing-change:rout-20230401-0923, s3:s3://redwood-incidents/1839501123/, ticket:MLP-4213.
